definitions.explanation: Describes things that lack uniformity in size, shape, quality, or alignment. Can refer to physical objects that do not match, or figuratively to a group of people with varied abilities or backgrounds.

examples.japanese: {不揃|ふぞろ}いな{野菜|やさい}を{安|やす}く{売|う}っている。
examples.english: They are selling irregularly shaped vegetables cheaply.

examples.japanese: {歯並|はなら}びが{不揃|ふぞろ}いで{気|き}にしている。
examples.english: I am self-conscious about my uneven teeth.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きさが{不揃|ふぞろ}いだが、{味|あじ}は{変|か}わらないので{問題|もんだい}ない。
examples.english: The sizes are irregular, but the taste is the same so there is no problem.

notes:
USAGE: {不揃|ふぞろ}い describes a lack of uniformity. It is frequently used for produce, teeth, hair, handwriting, and other things expected to be even or matched.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大|おお}きさが{不揃|ふぞろ}い (irregular in size)
- {不揃|ふぞろ}いな{野菜|やさい} (irregularly shaped vegetables)
- {歯並|はなら}びが{不揃|ふぞろ}い (uneven teeth)
- {不揃|ふぞろ}いの{林檎|りんご}たち ("Imperfect Apples" — a famous 1983 TV drama title)

CULTURAL NOTE: {不揃|ふぞろ}い{野菜|やさい} (irregularly shaped produce) has become a positive concept in recent years, as consumers embrace imperfect vegetables to reduce food waste.
